review_basis: Seventh ORVYQ system-owned claim-specific visual-QA round. Each target asset is a repository-owned derivative whose video SHA-256 is identical to an already byte-bound and provenance-approved NOAA source clip. The target contact-sheet identity is bound to the exact current queue entry. Approval is limited to the stated contextual use; maps, source documents and primary evidence retain all location, quantitative, institutional and legal factual burdens.

decisions.reason: The identical approved NOAA deep-sea footage provides genuine dark-ocean physical scale for the abyssal narration. It is used only as contextual deep-water imagery and is never presented as the Clarion-Clipperton Zone, polymetallic nodules, or evidence of a measured condition.

The identical approved NOAA clip visibly shows scientists deploying an ROV from a research vessel and therefore supports real marine field-operation scale. It must not identify the vessel as Chikyu or depict the exact Japanese pumping system; official evidence carries those claims.

The identical approved NOAA ROV-operations footage supplies authentic deep-seabed observation context and avoids tropical or decorative imagery. It does not itself prove track persistence; the cited scientific evidence retains the measured historical claim.

The identical approved NOAA expedition footage provides a real survey and field-assessment setting that clearly differs from a commercial mine. It is not identified as Chikyu, a Japanese trial vessel, or proof of commercial feasibility.

The identical approved NOAA water-column footage supplies real ocean depth and darkness for the closing physical metaphor. It introduces no new location, species, legal, or quantitative claim and avoids artificial science-fiction imagery.
